title: Spring Boot and REST APIs — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: Expose the expense tracker as a REST service. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which status fits a successful resource creation?
questions.explanation: Creation commonly includes a Location for the new resource.

questions.prompt: Why use response DTOs instead of returning JPA entities directly?

options.text: To control the external API and avoid persistence leakage

questions.explanation: DTOs keep API contracts separate from storage models.

questions.prompt: Which annotation requests validation of a bound request DTO?
questions.explanation: Jakarta validation constraints are applied through the configured validation integration.

questions.prompt: What status fits an unknown expense identifier?
questions.explanation: The requested resource does not exist.

questions.prompt: Why bound an API page size?

options.text: To control resource use and response size

questions.explanation: Unbounded collection requests can exhaust application and database capacity.

questions.prompt: Why is renaming a response field a compatibility decision?

options.text: External clients may depend on its name

questions.explanation: Public contracts extend beyond the service source tree.
GET /greeting?name=Ada maps to greeting. The request parameter becomes name = Ada. The returned record becomes a JSON response with message = Hello Ada.
